These are different operational outcomes, not a controlled comparison of defenses.","classification":"comparison of reported facts","left_claim_ids":["CF-2"],"right_claim_ids":["CI-1"]},"editorial_inference":{"text":"Previously trusted access stops being reliable evidence of legitimate action when an attacker can steal, retain or borrow the signal that earned that trust. A valid credential establishes possession; an allowed network origin establishes a route. Neither alone establishes that a particular business action is authorized. For leaders, the practical question is whether the sensitive action has its own enforceable authorization checks, even when the request arrives through an accepted account or network path.","claim_ids":["CF-1","CI-1","CI-2"]},"hypothetical_illustration":null,"causal_boundary":"These accounts cannot establish that segmentation caused the outcome difference, that any recommended control would have prevented the financial losses, or that the incidents shared an attacker.
